sports-bar.definition: A bar or restaurant designed around watching sports, often with many television screens.
sports-bar.exampleUsage: The hospitality glossary describes a sports bar as a venue centered on televised sports.

dive-bar.definition: An informal term for a simple, unpretentious neighborhood bar, often with basic décor and lower prices.
dive-bar.exampleUsage: The cultural glossary defines a dive bar as an informal type of bar.

wine-bar.definition: An establishment devoted exclusively to serving wine.
wine-bar.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Wine Bar" in an educational description.

rooftop-bar.definition: A bar located on a building's roof or upper terrace.
rooftop-bar.exampleUsage: The architecture guide identifies a rooftop bar as an upper-level hospitality space.

tiki-bar.definition: A themed bar decorated with imagery inspired by an imagined tropical or Polynesian style.
tiki-bar.exampleUsage: The design history lesson discusses the decorative style of a tiki bar.

pub.definition: Tavern consisting of a building with a bar and public rooms.

tavern.definition: A building with a bar that is licensed to sell alcoholic drinks.

lounge.definition: An upholstered seat for more than one person.

happy-hour.definition: A period when a bar offers alcoholic drinks for less than usual.

last-call.definition: An announcement in a bar or licensed venue that alcohol service will soon end according to venue rules or law.
last-call.exampleUsage: The hospitality glossary defines last call as an end-of-service announcement.
last-call.arabicTranslation: إعلان قرب انتهاء تقديم المشروبات الكحولية

tab.definition: A page in a browser or a labelled section in a program.

round-of-drinks.definition: A set of drinks bought or served for everyone in a group, usually alcoholic.

toast.definition: A celebrity who receives much acclaim and attention.

cheers.definition: To spur on or encourage especially by cheers and shouts.

designated-driver.definition: A person who avoids drinking at a gathering so they can drive the other guests home safely.

bar-tab.definition: A running record of charges for items ordered at a bar, typically paid together later.
bar-tab.exampleUsage: The business glossary defines a bar tab as a running customer bill.

cover-charge.definition: A fixed fee is added by a restaurant or nightclub separately from the cost of food and drinks.

live-music.definition: Music performed in person by musicians rather than played only from a recording.
live-music.exampleUsage: The venue calendar lists live music on Friday.

karaoke.definition: Singing popular songs accompanied by a recording of an orchestra (usually in bars or nightclubs).

trivia-night.definition: A social event in which teams or individuals answer general-knowledge questions.
trivia-night.exampleUsage: The venue hosts a trivia night with general-knowledge questions.

dart-board.definition: A round wooden or cork board serves as the target players aim at when playing darts.

pool-table.definition: A large, heavy table covered with cloth and used for playing pool.

jukebox.definition: A cabinet containing an automatic record player.

comedy-night.definition: An event featuring live comedy performances.
comedy-night.exampleUsage: The entertainment calendar lists a comedy night.

open-mic.definition: An event where members of the public can sign up to perform music, comedy, poetry, or other short acts.
open-mic.exampleUsage: The community calendar includes an open-mic event.

dance-floor.definition: An open area intended for people to dance on.
dance-floor.exampleUsage: The venue has a dance floor near the stage.

big-screen.definition: A large display screen used for showing television, films, sports, or presentations.
big-screen.exampleUsage: The sports venue shows matches on a big screen.

moderation.definition: The action of lessening in severity or intensity.

ride-share.definition: A transport service arranged through a platform or service in which a driver provides a booked ride.
ride-share.exampleUsage: The venue safety poster mentions ride-share as a transport category.

water-break.definition: A pause during an activity to drink water and rest briefly.
water-break.exampleUsage: The event schedule included a water break.

know-your-limit.definition: A safety phrase used in adult alcohol-service contexts to encourage awareness of when consumption should stop.
know-your-limit.exampleUsage: The venue's adult-safety poster displayed the phrase 'Know your limit.'

pace-yourself.definition: A general phrase meaning to proceed at a controlled rate rather than too quickly; in adult bar contexts it can appear as a responsible-service message.
pace-yourself.exampleUsage: The responsible-service poster included the phrase 'Pace yourself.'

eat-before.definition: A phrase meaning to eat food before another planned activity; it can appear in adult hospitality safety messaging.
eat-before.exampleUsage: The poster included 'eat before' as part of an adult venue safety campaign.

id-check.definition: A process in which staff verify an identity document, often to confirm identity or legal age.
id-check.exampleUsage: The venue uses an ID check where age restrictions apply.

legal-age.definition: The age at which a person is legally recognized as able to make decisions and manage personal responsibilities independently.

cut-off.definition: In licensed alcohol service, the point when a venue refuses further alcohol service to a patron under safety rules or law.
cut-off.exampleUsage: The staff-training glossary defines cut-off as ending further alcohol service.
